message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I am p4 with $125 cash and two Get Out of Jail Free cards. I own a yellow monopoly with one house on each property, plus several unmortgaged orange and red properties. The opponent is p3.

The opponent has $1627 and owns a full dark blue monopoly, all four railroads, and several hotels. I have no mortgaged properties and no Get Out of Jail Free cards. I just paid $1100 rent on Pacific Avenue and mortgaged Park Place. I am deciding whether to end my turn or propose a trade with p3.

Selling the yellow houses would yield about $225. Mortgaging MEDITERRANEAN or NEW_YORK would add roughly $130. The opponent's light blue hotels, pink four-houses, and green four-houses are all major threats.

I am calculating the exact board positions to determine how far p3 must roll from Boardwalk to reach my yellow properties.

I mapped the full board. From Boardwalk, the opponent's next roll cannot land on any of my properties. The farthest they can reach is St. Charles with a 12, which belongs to them.

The opponent cannot land on my yellows for at least two rolls. They would need 27 spaces to reach them, while their nearest unmortgaged properties are only 16 to 20 spaces away.

The opponent is not an immediate threat from their movement. The real danger is my next roll from Pacific Avenue.

Rolling 2 lands on North Carolina with four houses, which would cost about $1050. Rolling 4 lands on Pennsylvania Avenue with four houses, another large rent. Rolling 5 hits the Short Line railroad for $200. Rolling 7 or 9 lands on mortgaged properties where I collect no rent. Rolling 10 hits GO for $200. Rolling 11 lands on Mediterranean, which is mine.

I am calculating the exact rent values for these green properties.

Standard Monopoly rent values are now confirmed. Rolling 2 on North Carolina costs $1100, and rolling 4 on Pennsylvania Avenue costs $1200. With only $125 cash, even mortgaging Mediterranean and New York for about $130, plus selling the three yellow houses for $225, yields roughly $480 total. That is still short of the required amount, so landing on either of those properties would bankrupt me.

Rolling 5 on Short Line costs $200, which I can cover with mortgaged properties and cash. Rolling 8 on Luxury Tax costs $100, which I can also pay. The only rolls that guarantee bankruptcy are 2 and 4, totaling four of thirty-six possible outcomes. Unmortgaging properties costs money rather than generating cash.

I am now considering whether to propose a trade with p3. They own all the properties that would bankrupt me, so they might be willing to trade them away for something in return.

The opponent has no incentive to trade. They are winning decisively and want me to land on the green properties and bankrupt. I have the only yellow monopoly, which they could use to complete a new set. I also own all three orange properties, though two are mortgaged. They do not need my dark blue properties since they already hold Boardwalk.

Trading away the yellow monopoly would eliminate my only income source and give the opponent another deadly set. They already own Baltic, so Mediterranean would complete a weak brown monopoly. I cannot trade for a green property to break their four-house green monopoly because they will never exchange it for anything I have. My net worth is far too small to threaten one green rent.

A rejected trade proposal would still consume my turn, so I must only offer deals that are actually worth accepting. I am now considering whether to ask for Illinois from the opponent.

I realized that trading for Illinois would not help. I already own Kentucky and Indiana, but both are mortgaged. Unmortgaging them would cost about $121 each plus interest, and I have no cash for building. A red monopoly is not an immediate survival tool.

I do not need to mortgage now. The engine lets me liquidate during the debt resolution phase after I roll, so I can wait until I actually owe money rather than locking in cash beforehand.

Pre-emptive mortgaging would not save me from the upcoming rolls, and it would reduce future income. New York Avenue and Mediterranean Avenue generate almost no rent while mortgaged, so keeping them unmortgaged offers little benefit. I also cannot build any houses right now because I have no cash for construction.

Unmortgaging the two orange properties would cost about $99 each, leaving me with no spare cash. Even with a full orange monopoly, the rent would only be roughly $32 per turn, which is not enough to survive the upcoming rolls.

Selling the yellow houses would cut my income from $110 to $44 per turn. I will keep them and end my turn.

I will pass this turn. I have no urgent need for jail cards, and the yellow monopoly is my only viable income source. The opponent is on Boardwalk and cannot reach my properties, so they pose no immediate threat. My turn will follow theirs, and I must survive the upcoming roll from Pacific Avenue.

A roll of 6 on the Chance space could land me on Illinois for $20, or on the nearest railroad for $200. Other cards like "pay poor tax" are manageable.

The opponent can reach Mediterranean Avenue in one roll from Boardwalk. I will mortgage it now so they collect no rent.
